title: 31.1 An Inductor-Less Capacitor-Less Synchronous Piezoelectric-Electromagnetic Hybrid Energy Harvesting Platform with Coil-Sharing Scheme
problem: Energy harvesting for IoT and edge AI devices requires multiple discrete or on-chip power components (inductors, capacitors) across rectification, DC-DC conversion, and regulation stages, increasing system volume, cost, and area.
motivation: Eliminating external power components through clever circuit design enables fully integrated energy-harvesting solutions that are smaller, cheaper, and more efficient for battery-less IoT and edge AI devices.
method: The platform combines two types of energy harvesters—piezoelectric (which converts vibration into electricity through material deformation) and electromagnetic (which converts motion into electricity using a coil in a magnetic field). Rather than using separate inductors and capacitors (electronic components that store and regulate electrical energy) at each power-conversion stage, it reuses the electromagnetic coil as a shared inductor for all three stages: rectification (converting AC to DC power), DC-DC conversion (adjusting voltage levels), and regulation (stabilizing the output voltage). This coil-sharing synchronous rectification scheme means one component does multiple jobs, eliminating the need for external inductors and capacitors.
key_novelty: A coil-sharing scheme that eliminates external inductors and capacitors by reusing the electromagnetic harvester's coil across all power-conversion stages.
contributions: Hybrid PE-EM energy harvesting on single platform

metrics.other: system volume reduction, cost reduction, integration

baselines: prior designs with external inductors and capacitors
primary_theme: Fully integrated hybrid energy harvesting with coil-sharing
